title: A notebook is not a tidy chronology
documented: The V&A holds five notebooks bound in three volumes. Their surviving binding is not a reliable chronological order; the institution identifies notes about water, weights and geometry among the contents.
looking: Open the museum’s page viewer. Follow a diagram and its neighboring writing, then compare another page. Record which relationship is actually visible and which depends on the cataloguer’s explanation.
limit: A present-day page sequence cannot establish the order of every idea. These are linked institutional viewers; their images have not been copied into our collection.

title: Investigation can include rejection
documented: The V&A discusses Leonardo’s investigation and eventual rejection of perpetual motion. The notebook brings mathematical and mechanical questions into the same physical working object.
looking: Use the institutional viewer to examine folio 91 verso. Distinguish a diagram’s proposal from evidence that a machine worked. Consider what would have to be tested before accepting the design.
limit: The museum’s account concerns the investigation; it does not supply a successful perpetual-motion mechanism. No animated reconstruction here pretends otherwise.
